# Agile Manifesto

> The foundational declaration of agile software development values and principles, created by 17 pioneering software thought leaders in 2001.

The Agile Manifesto is the seminal document that defined agile software development methodology through four core values and twelve guiding principles. It has been translated into numerous languages and remains the cornerstone reference for agile practices worldwide.

## Key Topics

- Agile Manifesto
- Core Values
- Twelve Principles
- Software Development
- Iterative Development
- Customer Collaboration
- Agile Methodology
- Kent Beck
- Martin Fowler
- Alistair Cockburn
- Manifesto Signatories
- Agile Principles
- Software Engineering
- Methodology
- Manifesto Declaration

## Core Manifesto

- [Manifesto for Agile Software Development](https://agilemanifesto.org/iso/en/manifesto.html): Original Agile Manifesto founding document with core values
- [Principles behind the Agile Manifesto](https://agilemanifesto.org/principles.html): Twelve core principles underlying the Agile Manifesto values

## History & Signatories

- [History: The Agile Manifesto](https://agilemanifesto.org/history.html): History of Agile Manifesto creation at Snowbird, Utah in 2001
- [Signatories: The Agile Manifesto](https://agilemanifesto.org/authors.html): Manifesto creators including Kent Beck, Mike Beedle, Scrum and XP pioneers
- [Agile Manifesto Signatories](https://agilemanifesto.org/display/index.html): List of signatories who created the Agile Manifesto
